decision: ContinuumOS is a vendor-neutral care-orchestration overlay and not a system-of-record replacement.
rationale: The case addresses fragmented responsibility and workflow visibility while preserving EHR LIS RIS/PACS and other source-system roles.
scope_impact: Prevents EHR replacement scope and keeps source-of-truth mapping explicit.
review_trigger: Review only if the approved product boundary changes.

decision: Use a SMART on FHIR launch demonstration with limited synthetic FHIR data.
rationale: This gives a clinician-facing entry into the synthetic episode without claiming a production interoperability implementation.
scope_impact: Limits the case to a high-level launch demonstration; detailed scopes field mapping and implementation design are deferred.

decision: Use the diagnostic-closure and care-escalation wedge from order through human-confirmed next step.
rationale: The wedge is narrow enough for a seven-day case and exposes the core result-to-action ownership gap.
scope_impact: Allows clinic management day-care referral and hospital escalation; excludes surgery discharge and home recovery.
review_trigger: Review only if the MVP start or end boundary changes.

decision: Use synthetic data and simulated integrations only.
rationale: The portfolio case must not use real patient payer provider or credential information.
scope_impact: All source records AI evaluations and scenario evidence remain synthetic.
review_trigger: Review only with explicit approved data-governance scope change.

decision: Use deterministic rules for predictable workflow conditions and reserve MVP AI for source-linked synthesis and human-approved referral-handoff preparation.
rationale: Missing owner missed SLA overdue acknowledgement and duplicate indicators are more transparent as rules; the MVP AI adds value for source-linked context and handoff preparation.
scope_impact: Prevents simple deterministic checks and hidden prioritisation from being misrepresented as MVP AI capability.
review_trigger: Review if a capability changes decision rights or safety controls.

decision: Use two MVP AI capabilities: source-linked episode summary and referral handoff draft after human-approved referral or escalation.
rationale: The summary makes episode facts, status, report version, open tasks and missing or conflicting source information visible. The draft supports preparation only after a human approves the referral direction.
scope_impact: Operational-attention recommendations remain roadmap or optional evaluation material; autonomous diagnosis clinical prioritisation referral approval and financial authorisation remain excluded.
review_trigger: Review after synthetic evaluation evidence is available.

decision: Require human approval before an AI handoff package or patient-facing clinical content is used operationally.
rationale: AI drafts may assist preparation but cannot authorise referral routing or patient communication.
scope_impact: The Referral Coordinator approves an operational handoff package; the clinic physician approves patient-facing clinical content where clinical context is present. Approval, correction, rejection and override evidence are required.
accountable_owner: Product owner; Referral Coordinator for handoff; Clinic physician for clinical content
review_trigger: Review only if governance requirements become more restrictive.

decision: Treat an enterprise event platform as architecture context only.
rationale: Kafka Flink and similar technologies do not need to be built to demonstrate the product case.
scope_impact: No enterprise event backbone is implemented in the seven-day case.

decision: Treat a longitudinal record as a future product option and not the primary clinical record for this MVP.
rationale: The case needs a shared workflow view not a replacement clinical repository.
scope_impact: Keeps longitudinal data-platform work out of the current scope.

decision: Use human-confirmed diagnostic next step within the defined workflow SLA and supporting safety workflow and AI evaluation measures.
rationale: The measurement model must show diagnostic closure while preventing speed claims from masking unsafe linkage incomplete audit evidence or missing human approval.
scope_impact: Defines metrics as calculation methods and validation requirements; no baseline target or achieved outcome is claimed.
accountable_owner: Product owner with Care Coordinator representative
review_trigger: Review when synthetic acceptance evidence and policy-defined thresholds are available.

decision: Use Commure SuperOS Philips MIOT/IASORA and openEHR only as external design and architecture references.
rationale: ContinuumOS is an independent vendor-neutral product case. Reference patterns may inform framing but their capabilities integrations outcomes or implementation maturity must not be claimed as ContinuumOS work.
scope_impact: Protects the portfolio case from borrowed-credibility claims and prevents vendor-specific scope or implementation assumptions.
review_trigger: Review before any external-facing artifact cites or compares a vendor reference.

decision: For urgent, human-approved hospital escalation, allow Next Step Confirmed while Financial Readiness Pending remains visible and unresolved once clinical direction, receiving-team handoff, accountable owner, timeframe and patient communication are confirmed.
rationale: Urgent clinical progression must not be blocked by supporting administrative readiness work.
scope_impact: Adds a controlled urgent branch from Referral Accepted to Next Step Confirmed; financial readiness remains visible and is not treated as complete.
accountable_owner: Clinic physician and receiving team for human gates; Care Coordinator for closure evidence
decision_status: Recorded for Sprint 2 alignment; not implemented
review_trigger: Requires clinical, operational and financial review before implementation.

decision: Treat MVP AI support as optional to canonical workflow progression and fall back to source evidence and the normal human workflow when AI fails, times out or is unavailable.
rationale: The two AI capabilities are assistive and must not become dependencies for acknowledgement, care direction, handoff, receiving response or closure.
scope_impact: Requires visible AI failure evidence and a non-blocking human fallback; does not add an AI or workflow capability.
accountable_owner: Product owner; accountable workflow owner for fallback
decision_status: Recorded during Sprint 4 architecture alignment; not implemented
review_trigger: Review if an AI output is proposed as a mandatory workflow prerequisite.

decision: For the approved synthetic fixture, require an accepted current DiagnosticReport status (final, amended or corrected), the current source version, resolution of configured required result references and separate source-specific completion evidence before Result Available; Observation or preliminary/partial evidence alone is insufficient.
rationale: A structured Observation or preliminary/partial report can exist without a complete, current or reviewable diagnostic report.
scope_impact: Refines T04/E04 as a fixture completion rule, not a universal FHIR requirement; incomplete or inconsistent configured evidence routes to Result Incomplete.
accountable_owner: Diagnostic operations user; authorised reporting source
decision_status: Recorded during Sprint 4 architecture alignment; not implemented
review_trigger: Review during UAT and before adapting the demonstration to a source with a different report-status policy.

decision: Apply minimum-necessary data to source retrieval, display, internal retention, audit payloads and AI inputs.
rationale: Least privilege does not by itself prevent unnecessary copying of complete clinical records.
scope_impact: ContinuumOS retains only scoped synthetic orchestration and evidence fields and references source records rather than becoming a duplicate clinical repository.
accountable_owner: Product owner; product/platform administrator for design controls
decision_status: Recorded during Sprint 4 architecture alignment; not implemented
review_trigger: Review if a new field, full-document copy or expanded AI input is proposed.

decision: Use append-oriented, attributable and target tamper-evident workflow evidence; corrections create linked correction or superseding entries rather than destructive edits.
rationale: The audit model must preserve history while allowing accountable correction without silently overwriting prior evidence.
scope_impact: Refines the audit target across architecture, event, data and prototype trace designs; it does not claim implemented immutability or tamper evidence.
decision_status: Recorded during Sprint 4 architecture alignment; not implemented
review_trigger: Review when the audit schema, retention and technical integrity controls are designed.

decision: Separate communication preparation, approval, send attempt, delivery, failure, follow-up and explicit patient confirmation; sent or delivered does not prove understanding or acceptance.
rationale: Communication transport status and patient confirmation have different evidence meaning and owners.
scope_impact: Prevents notification events from independently satisfying Next Step Confirmed or Episode Completed.
accountable_owner: Clinic physician for clinical content; authorised communication owner; Care Coordinator for closure evidence
decision_status: Recorded during Sprint 4 architecture alignment; not implemented
review_trigger: Review when message policy, patient-confirmation requirements and UAT cases are defined.

decision: Require a defined linkage contract before episode attachment or progression, including identifiers, source references, Encounter requirements, version handling, permitted manual reconciliation and accountable resolver.
rationale: The phrase verified linkage is unsafe unless its evidence and authority are explicit.
scope_impact: Manual reconciliation may establish an internal reference but cannot silently alter source identity or encounter records.
decision_status: Recorded during Sprint 4 architecture alignment; not implemented
review_trigger: Review when the SMART sequence, event catalogue and linkage test cases are defined.
